newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses hit records, gold slips on fund.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses hit records, gold slips on fund.

text.p: Major European bourses rebounded to hit record levels on Wednesday after U.S. central bank head Alan Greenspan soothed investors' worst fears, at least for now.

The London and Paris stock markets scored new highs by mid-afternoon after Greenspan, who has spooked investors on various occasions with warning comments, again denied he was trying to talk Wall Street down.
He said current share price levels could be justified if earnings forecasts were right.
In Frankfurt, shares rose further in after-hours electronic trading to add to a record close in earlier floor trade.
Wall Street also took heart from Greenspan's comments, with the Dow Jones industrial average gaining around half a percent after an hour of trading.

But the chairman of the U.S. Federal Reserve, who sent stocks tumbling a week ago with a warning that Wall Street's rise had "raised questions of sustainability", was due to give yet another speech later on Wednesday.
Greenspan was due to give the second leg of his Humphrey-Hawkins Congressional testimony at 1900 GMT.
Gold slid to trade around $354, down almost $6 from the previous London close, on news of Swiss plans to sell gold from reserves to finance a fund for Holocaust victims and others.
Bullion analysts said the amount involved was unlikely to be large compared with overall market turnover, but the news added to the pressure on gold.
"The amount is not huge by any means but it is indicative of central bank sentiment towards the market," one dealer said.
Concern that central banks would sell gold to help meet the economic criteria for joining European economic and monetary union had dented the gold price before its recent rebound.

On currency markets, meanwhile, the dollar traded below a new 34-month peak against the German currency of 1.7169 marks, hit in Asian business, and lost some ground against a firm Japanese yen at around 121.40 yen.

Traders said comments on Tuesday by Bundesbank council member Guntram Palm that recent mark movements were still an "appropriate correction" lessened the attraction of the mark, already depressed by weakness in the German economy.

"Generally poor sentiment toward the mark remains and Palm's comments seemed to give its recent bout of weakness a pat on the back," said Peter Wood, currency trader at Bank of Boston. Comments by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin that a strong dollar was in U.S. interests but that it had been strong for "quite some time" and that the United States was watching the trade deficit with Japan gave support to the yen.

Japanese government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama, meanwhile, said Tokyo needed to consider how to deal with the impact of low interest rates on incomes -- making the market more nervous about how long Japanese interest rates can remain low.

The London stock market, Europe's busiest, opened lower after a 66-point fall in the Dow Jones industrial average in New York overnight and in reaction to some disappointing corporate results. But Greenspan's reassuring comments later helped the market climb into previously uncharted territory.

British Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George held their monthly monetary meeting on Wednesday but, as expected this close to an election due by May, the central bank left official interest rates unchanged.
In Frankfurt shares showed no signs of any hangover from Tuesday's record-breaking run, boosted by a steady dollar, which is good news for German exporters.

"There are some decent volumes there and the greenback is helping, especially with the exporters. The slogan at the moment seems to be -- enjoy it and let the cash roll in," said Josh Waiblinger of equity sales at BHF Bank.
The Paris bourse set an all-time high after a renewed rally which followed Greenspan's remarks and was fuelled by a firm dollar, dealers said.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7120 marks and 121.42 yen, compared with 1.7118 and 121.94 late on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 4.5 points at 4,362.2 after earlier hitting a record 4,367.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 gained 18.59 to 2,670.28 after an earlier record 2,676.55.

FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended floor trade up 44.33 at a record close of 3,364.99, near an all-time high during the session of 3,365.03, and rose further to around 3,377 in later computerised trading.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $354.50 versus $355.75 in the morning and well down from the previous London close of $359.80 before dropping to around $354. Silver slipped three cents to $5.22.
